text:
The defendant would most likely be guilty of murder where they acted with malice aforethought—intent to kill, intent to cause serious bodily harm, or reckless indifference to an unjustifiably high risk to human life—and death resulted, or where a death occurred during an inherently dangerous felony under the felony murder rule. Lending a car to a person known to be severely intoxicated can also support murder liability, since that extreme recklessness and conscious disregard for human life directly causes any resulting death.
CONFIDENCE: 90
